step: Fix: the picture of a moved original (fixed) macOS window

report.user: при движении окна в macos картинка игры не двигается вместе с окном (with a screenshot)
report.screenshot: a VS match in the window 'Little Fighter 2' with a 794-point client at 2x (1588 px wide): the picture at one point per game pixel, shifted up and left by about 297 x 53 game pixels (the first HUD row and 1.5 panels cut off), black to the right and bottom. 794 points is the original fixed window, not the scalable one (1588 points at 2x on this display); how it was launched (--original-window, the NTSDOriginalWindow default or an older build) is not known

cause.summary: The original fixed window follows its live geometry: the display backend crops the desktop-sized primary at the window's live client, and clips the game's Blt there, while the game Blts at the rectangle its WM_MOVE handler stored at 453ccc. The macOS host sent WM_MOVE once, at startup, so after a move the crop moved and the drawing did not: the picture showed shifted by the move, black (fresh known-black primary) beyond. The scalable window (default since S3) is not affected: its geometry is held from creation.
code_at_94581233: native/Sources/NTSDRuntime/OriginalMacDisplayBackend.swift:567-578 rectangle(): the primary's delivery and clip rectangle from windows.displayGeometry(window) (572), i.e. the live client for a window without a hold
native/Sources/NTSDRuntime/OriginalMacDisplayBackend.swift:1102-1103 frontTarget(): the game's Blt destination intersected with that live rectangle
native/Sources/NTSDMacPlatform/OriginalMacWindowBackend.swift:172-176 displayGeometry(): the live window's client on the screen
native/Sources/NTSDCore/OriginalWindowLifecycle.swift:55-62 WM_MOVE (43b3d0 case 3, windowed): GetClientRect and two ClientToScreen stored at 453ccc
native/Sources/NTSDRuntime/OriginalMacRuntimeMenu.swift:103-109 the only WM_MOVE: posted once at startup; nothing observed the window's moves (no didMove handling anywhere in the macOS host)

change.NTSDRuntime/OriginalMacRuntimeMessages: move(origin): WM_MOVE with the client's desktop origin in lParam, only when it differs from the last one posted; a pending WM_MOVE takes the new origin instead of queueing another (its handler re-reads the live geometry)
change.NTSDRuntime/OriginalMacRuntimeMenu: the startup WM_MOVE goes through move() (same message); windowMoved(token,in:) sends it for the current window when it follows its live geometry (not closed, not the full-screen popup, no hold: scalable window and macOS full screen excluded)
change.NTSDMacPlatform/OriginalMacWindowBackend: setMoved(token,_): NSWindow.didMoveNotification observer, only on a window without a hold that is not the popup (the fixed window); removed with the window's other observers
change.NTSDApp/OriginalRuntimeLaunch: attach() installs it and checks once: after Alt+Enter the new, centred window sends WM_MOVE when the game last had another origin
change.unchanged: Core, the shared window backend, the display backend, the scalable window, timing, other hosts; no message is sent while the window stays where the game last was

unit.new: OriginalMacRuntimeMenuTests.testMovedWindowSendsWMMoveAndThePictureFollows: the live runtime menu on an AppKit window; an unchanged origin sends nothing; a 40x30 move without WM_MOVE presents the frame shifted (pixel(x,y) = unmoved(x+40,y+30), the right 40 columns and bottom 30 rows black) and 453ccc keeps the old rectangle (the cause); one WM_MOVE with the moved origin (a second notice adds nothing), its handler stores the moved rectangle and the next frame equals the unmoved one byte for byte; two AppKit moves before the game reads its queue leave one WM_MOVE with the latest origin; under a held geometry a move sends nothing

review: No independent review in this task; the parent agent reviews before merging.
boundaries: WM_MOVE is posted (and coalesced) when AppKit reports the move; Windows sends it during its modal move loop, in which the game does not run. Here the game keeps running while the window is dragged, and frames between the move and the game's next PeekMessage still show the old rectangle
A fixed window moved partly off the screen still stops at the geometry boundary (reproduced above; unchanged by this fix), as does a move to another display ('screen changed')

The SDL host's fixed window where positions are known (X11, macOS SDL, Windows) uses the same model (SDLWindows.swift origin() is the live position) and handles no move event: probably the same bug, not checked or changed here

Seen while checking, not caused by this change (the popup path is untouched) and not rerun on the previous build: in a live run the game's own full-screen popup (Alt+Enter) did not take a second Alt+Enter, posted to the process or through the HID stream; the borderless popup probably cannot become key
